summary: Hosted streaming disconnects + questions on SLO accounting (client abort vs server-side stream failure)
description:
Customer (Northstar Financial) reports intermittent streaming disconnects on Hosted chat/completions and is asking how Redwood classifies them for reliability/SLO reporting.

Customer notes:
- They consume streaming via SSE.
- They observe occasional "stream ended"/disconnect mid-generation with no final message.
- They suspect some are caused by client-side timeouts/proxies, but are concerned Redwood counts these as platform errors.
- They want a clear definition of: (a) what counts as a streaming failure, (b) what is excluded as client abort, and (c) whether disconnects impact availability/error-rate SLI.

Impact:
- User-facing partial responses in their app (Hosted).
- Questions are blocking internal rollout and their security/reliability review.

Requested from Support:
- Clarify Redwood SLI/SLO accounting for streaming disconnects.
- Provide guidance on what they should log/collect to distinguish client aborts vs server-side terminations.

Internal context:
- Ongoing tiered SLO + error budget program; streaming reliability is a primary SLI with explicit exclusions (client aborts, invalid requests, rate-limited requests).
- Need to ensure external wording matches measurement reality and avoids implying Redwood is accountable for client-side network drops.
comments:
2026-02-11 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Intake
Customer says: "We see streaming responses terminate unexpectedly ~0.3–0.8% of requests (varies by hour). We cannot tell if this is our ALB/proxy or Redwood. How do you count streaming disconnects for SLO? Do these show up as 5xx?" Requested examples and asked customer for request IDs + timestamps + region.

Asked customer to provide:
- Request IDs (x-redwood-request-id) for 10–20 failures
- Timestamps (UTC) and region
- Client error message + HTTP status (if any)
- Whether they received any SSE event indicating a server error vs silent disconnect
- Their client read timeout / proxy idle timeout settings

Set priority P2 (customer rollout concern, no clear Sev1 platform incident indicators).

2026-02-11 (Aisha Bello, SRE) — Initial guidance on classification
High-level SLI semantics (internal):
- Availability / success-rate SLI uses request-level outcome at gateway: counts as success when request completes with non-5xx and (for streaming) reaches terminal completion event; 429/4xx excluded by definition; explicit exclusions for client aborts.
- Streaming reliability SLI is measured via stream lifecycle events:
  - stream_opened
  - stream_completed (terminal)
  - stream_error (terminal)
  - client_abort (terminal, excluded)

If the connection is closed by the client (e.g., client cancels request, upstream proxy drops idle connection), we attempt to classify as client_abort and exclude from SLI. If the server terminates due to internal error, upstream model server failure, or gateway timeout, it is stream_error and counts against SLI.

Potential gray area: network resets where the gateway only sees a TCP reset without clear initiator. We’ve been improving taxonomy; some resets may currently be conservatively counted as stream_error if we can’t attribute to client. We should verify with sample request IDs.

Action: once we have request IDs, check gateway logs + stream termination reason tags in telemetry to see distribution (client_abort vs upstream_reset vs gateway_timeout).

2026-02-12 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Customer examples received
Customer sent 14 request IDs across us-east and eu-west. Their client stack: Node.js fetch + corporate proxy in front of app servers. They found their proxy has a 60s idle timeout and they sometimes generate >60s responses for long prompts.

Notable: several failures occur around 58–62s wall time.

Shared internally:
- request_id list attached in Zendesk side channel (not pasted here)
- sample: prompt length ~9k tokens, max_tokens=2048, streaming=true

2026-02-12 (Sergio Costa, Eng Platform - Dashboards/Alerts) — Quick look in logs/metrics
Pulled traces for 6 of the request IDs.
Findings:
- 4/6 show termination reason=client_disconnect (gateway saw downstream close) at ~60s.
- 1/6 shows upstream model server reset (reason=upstream_reset) around 12s; gateway returned no 5xx because stream was already open; stream_error emitted.
- 1/6 shows gateway idle timeout (reason=gateway_write_timeout) at ~65s; stream_error emitted.

So: majority appear client/proxy timeout; 2 look like platform-side stream errors.

Note: For the client_disconnect cases, we are emitting client_abort terminal event and excluding those from SLI accounting. For upstream_reset and gateway_write_timeout, these count against streaming reliability SLI.

Recommendation to customer: increase proxy idle timeout and/or send keep-alive comments (if supported) / reduce max_tokens / enforce server-side max stream duration. Also capture Redwood request_id for correlation.

Internal follow-up: ensure external docs clearly state that client disconnects are excluded; ambiguous resets may count if attribution is unclear.

2026-02-13 (Aisha Bello, SRE) — Customer-facing explanation drafted
Proposed response to customer (approved by Support):
1) What counts as a streaming failure: If Redwood terminates an active stream due to server-side error (upstream reset, gateway timeout, internal exception), we count that as a streaming reliability failure.
2) What is excluded: If the client closes the connection / cancels the request / downstream proxy times out, we classify as client abort and exclude from SLO/SLI calculations.
3) How it relates to 5xx: Not all streaming failures manifest as a single 5xx status code because the stream is already established; we track these via stream terminal events (completed/error/client-abort).
4) How to troubleshoot: Provide request IDs and timestamps; check client/proxy idle timeouts; consider setting max_tokens and enforcing app-level timeouts.

Also noted (transparent): In some rare cases where we cannot reliably attribute the disconnect initiator (e.g., certain TCP resets), we may conservatively treat it as a stream error. We are improving termination attribution and taxonomy as part of the tiered SLI work.

Linked internal references:
- SLI spec: sli-specification-api-gateway-and-routing
- Tiered SLO definitions (for internal alignment): tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated

Asked Sergio to confirm the two platform-side failures are not part of a broader incident (looked isolated).

2026-02-13 (Rachel Kim, Support) — Sent response + mitigation steps
Sent explanation to customer plus recommended mitigations:
- Increase proxy idle timeout above worst-case generation duration (suggest 3–5 minutes if they allow long outputs)
- Reduce max_tokens and/or use shorter prompts to avoid >60s streams
- Ensure the client continues reading from the stream; avoid buffering that can appear idle
- Log and pass through x-redwood-request-id for each request

Also offered: We can provide a short "SLO accounting" blurb suitable for their internal review; pointed them to updated docs (in progress) and offered to hop on a call with Solutions Engineering if needed.

Customer reply: acknowledged proxy timeout likely culprit; asked if Redwood can send periodic keep-alive events. We replied: currently we don’t guarantee heartbeat events on every stream; best practice is to set proxy/client timeouts appropriately and keep responses bounded.

2026-02-14 (Aisha Bello, SRE) — Resolution + follow-ups
Resolution: Clarified SLI/SLO accounting for streaming disconnects; confirmed most observed disconnects were client-side proxy idle timeouts and are excluded from SLI as client aborts. Two platform-side stream errors identified (upstream_reset, gateway_write_timeout) were isolated and did not indicate a broader incident; they would count against streaming reliability SLI.

Follow-ups:
- Docs: add explicit section in customer-facing reliability docs clarifying streaming terminal events and exclusions (tracked under redwood-docs/pr-2211).
- Telemetry: evaluate whether any ambiguous disconnect reasons are being over-counted as stream_error; if so, improve classification/tags without increasing metric cardinality (roll into ongoing tiered SLI tagging work).

Marking ticket Resolved; waiting on customer confirmation not required.
resolution: Provided definition of how Redwood classifies streaming disconnects (client abort excluded; server-side terminations count), validated sample request IDs, identified primary cause as customer proxy idle timeout, and shared mitigations + documentation references.
